pass_a_gloss: In the middle of his days they will abandon him. We all who once became under the partridge the calling one— for he made voiceless not only through the previously mentioned things, but also through all simply the deceiving ones and as upon piety the godlessness calling upon doctrines contrary to the truth— but 'in the middle of his days' we have abandoned him. For all indeed his days are the days of this age— but since he drew us out of the present evil age Christ Jesus, therefore 'in the middle of his days' we have abandoned him. 'And at the end of him there will be folly. For when was he wise, that at the end of him he should become foolish? But we will say that he was wise— for 'the' serpent was the wisest of all the beasts of the earth which the Lord God made. Wise he was according to the thing said in Isaiah— 'For I will bring upon the mind the great one, the ruler of the Assyrians. And he said· by strength I will make, and by wisdom
